newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives gain two points in Scotland.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives gain two points in Scotland.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives gained two points to 14 percent as the Scottish National Party (SNP) dropped three to 23 percent and Labour lost two to 51 percent voter support in a new Scottish opinion poll.
The Liberal Democrats were up one to 10 percent in the weekly System Three poll published in the Herald newspaper on Wednesday.

Only three weeks before the May 1 general election, Prime Minister John Major's party is running at just over half its 26 percent vote in the 1992 election. Labour is up on a 39 percent vote in 1992 and the SNP marginally above its 22 percent share.
The poll was conducted in 40 of Scotland's 72 constituencies on April 5-6. Conservatives held 10 Scottish seats, Labour 49, Liberal Democrats nine, and SNP four in the outgoing parliament.
The poll took place after Blair came under fire last week for comparing the tax raising powers of any Scottish parliament to that of a lowly parish council.
